overview: File (1944) on postwar Taiwan currency planning: officials defer exchange-rate and redemption decisions to future State-Treasury-military consultation, plus a routing memo on older Japan economic files.

people.name: George H. Blakeslee
people.role: State Department official in TS; recipient of the April 24 memorandum

people.name: Abbot Low Moffat
people.role: State Department official in LA; sender of both memoranda

people.name: John Carter Vincent
people.role: State Department official whose objections to proposed Taiwan currency policy are conveyed

people.name: Henry R. Labouisse, Jr.
people.role: State Department official in the Division of European Affairs; recipient of the June 22 memorandum

people.name: M. E. B. (unidentified)
people.role: Staff member or typist identified by initials in the drafting notation

people.name: E. H. S. (unidentified)
people.role: Staff member identified by initials in the June memorandum’s office notation

subfiles.title: Memorandum on Taiwan currency policy
subfiles.about: Moffat conveys John Carter Vincent’s objections and suggested revisions concerning exchange-rate control and currency redemption under a prospective military government in Taiwan.
subfiles.summary: Vincent and Moffat defer Taiwan's postwar currency exchange-rate and redemption decisions to future State-Treasury-military talks.

subfiles.title: Routing memorandum on Japanese economic papers
subfiles.about: Moffat forwards older Defense Materials papers about Japanese economic matters for Labouisse’s use and eventual return to the central files.
subfiles.summary: Moffat forwards dated Japan-economics files that may still interest a colleague, before returning them to central files.

interest: Shows 1944 US planning for Taiwan's postwar currency transition from Japanese to Chinese money.
